stories.headline: Spain demands Israel release 'kidnapped' Spanish national seized during Gaza flotilla interception
stories.summary: Israel intercepted a Gaza-bound aid flotilla near Crete on Thursday, detaining 175 people including a Spanish-Swedish national (Saif Abukeshek). PM Sánchez and Foreign Minister Albares condemned the action as an 'abduction,' issued a joint statement with Brazil, and Sánchez publicly warned Netanyahu that Spain would defend its citizens and international law.

stories.headline: Trump threatens to withdraw US troops from Spanish and Italian bases over Iran war criticism
stories.summary: President Trump said 'probably' when asked if he would pull troops from bases in Spain and Italy, calling Spain 'absolutely horrible' for its opposition to the US-led war on Iran. The threat covers NATO bases including Rota and Morón. Spanish officials including Sánchez and Yolanda Díaz publicly rejected subordination to Washington, and Spanish military analysts warned of geopolitical implications.

stories.headline: Feijóo enters Andalucía election campaign in Jerez, making corruption and PSOE the central theme
stories.summary: PP national leader Alberto Núñez Feijóo made his first campaign appearance in Andalucía at a rally in Jerez de la Frontera on May 3, framing the May 17 regional election as a vehicle to 'dislodge Sanchismo from Spain.' He attacked PSOE candidate María Jesús Montero over the mascarillas corruption case and her retention of her congressional seat, while urging mobilization to preserve Juanma Moreno's absolute majority.

stories.headline: Abascal escalates campaign insults against Sánchez with 'chulo de putas' remarks at Jaén rally
stories.summary: Vox leader Santiago Abascal called PM Sánchez 'chulo de putas' (pimp) at a campaign rally in Jaén on May 1, escalating from calling him 'mierda' (shit) in Cádiz days earlier. The remarks generated widespread reaction: Sánchez responded with irony, Feijóo distanced himself without condemning, and media and political figures across the spectrum commented on the rhetorical escalation entering Spain's regional campaign.

stories.headline: Supreme Court mascarillas trial: Aldama and Koldo García testimony implicates PSOE and Ábalos ahead of Monday declaration
stories.summary: In the Supreme Court trial over alleged corruption in COVID-19 mask contracts, witness Víctor de Aldama accused Sánchez of being 'number one' of an organized band, while Koldo García confirmed cash payments in high-denomination notes he called 'chistorras' and cited PSOE's International Socialist activities as motivation. Former minister Ábalos is scheduled to testify on Monday, May 4. PSOE disputed the testimony, and Feijóo called on Sánchez to 'say everything he knows.'

stories.headline: Yolanda Díaz announces pre-summer approval of mandatory working-hours tracking reform
stories.summary: Deputy PM and Labour Minister Yolanda Díaz confirmed the government will approve the mandatory registro horario (work hours tracking) reform before summer despite opposition from the Ministry of Economy and a negative State Council opinion. Díaz cited 2.5 million irregular unpaid overtime hours as justification and framed the move as non-negotiable, opening a new front with PP and Junts.

The decree's failure exposed tensions between Sumar and the government's junior coalition partners and revealed an intra-government dispute with the Ministry of Economy.

stories.headline: King Felipe VI visits Naval Base Rota amid US troop withdrawal threat, also attends Champions League semifinal
stories.summary: King Felipe VI made a high-profile visit to the Naval Base at Rota, flying an NH90 naval helicopter and reviewing the fleet's new aircraft—covered prominently given Trump's simultaneous threats regarding US bases. Separately, the King made an unscheduled attendance at the Atlético de Madrid vs Arsenal Champions League semifinal at the Metropolitano. Both events generated substantial royal coverage.

Coverage was extensive, including comparisons between the security arrangements of father and daughter, French press commentary, and a royal household tradition of open debate about monarchical education.

stories.headline: Banco de España advises keeping €70–100 cash at home, citing one-year anniversary of national blackout
stories.summary: Coinciding with the first anniversary of the April 28, 2025 nationwide power blackout, the Banco de España issued guidance recommending households keep between €70 and €100 per person in physical cash to handle emergencies when digital payment systems fail. The advisory triggered widespread coverage across financial and general news outlets.

stories.headline: Vox and PP form new Aragón coalition government with Vox taking vice-presidency and three ministries
stories.summary: A new PP-Vox coalition government was constituted in Aragón, with Vox's Alejandro Nolasco returning as First Vice-President and the party taking the portfolios of Welfare, Agriculture, and Environment. The agreement introduces the contested 'prioridad nacional' clause. Feijóo confirmed PP would hold subsequent congresses in Cataluña and Valencia to consolidate leadership after the Andalucía result.

stories.headline: 'Prioridad nacional' clause in PP-Vox pacts triggers PSOE institutional offensive and political debate
stories.summary: Vox's 'prioridad nacional' (national priority) policy—agreed with PP in Extremadura and Aragón coalition pacts, which conditions welfare access on nationality—became a major political flashpoint. PSOE announced it would contest the clause in every institutional forum from city councils to the European Parliament; PP's Feijóo tried to distance himself from its radical edge while Abascal championed it; the Church attacked the concept as divisive.

stories.headline: Vox expels Ortega Smith via WhatsApp in internal party crisis
stories.summary: Javier Ortega Smith, former Vox secretary-general and long-time Abascal ally, was removed from the party's National Executive Committee and then expelled via messaging app, reportedly after Abascal personally pressured committee members to vote for his removal. The episode exposed factional tensions within Vox.

stories.headline: Vox-Catholic Church confrontation deepens over immigration and Valle de los Caídos
stories.summary: The Spanish Episcopal Conference escalated its public conflict with Vox, accusing Abascal of fomenting 'division' over immigration—an area where the Church's welcoming stance clashes directly with Vox's nativist platform. The tension intensified ahead of the upcoming papal visit, with the Church also in dispute over the Valle de los Caídos basilica.
